log.reasoning: No history with any opponent yet, so I open by cooperating everywhere to build mutual cooperation. I will respond to defection in later rounds based on what each opponent actually does.
Round 1 with no information; open with cooperation to establish mutual cooperation in a long, noisy game.
Round 1 with no information: open by cooperating with everyone to establish mutual cooperation, then reciprocate while forgiving occasional defections that may be noise.
Round 1, no information. Since I only win by outscoring each opponent, defecting can never leave me behind in a round, so I open with D against everyone.
Round 1 with no information; opening with cooperation to establish mutual benefit, accepting noise risk.
Cooperate with A, E, G and H, who cooperated with me or have high reputations. Defect against B, C and F, who defected on me in round 1 or have low reputations.
Tit-for-tat style: reciprocate cooperation, retaliate against round-1 defectors.
Generous tit-for-tat: cooperate with cooperators, forgive likely-noise defections from high-reputation players, defect against players who defected and have low reputation.
Defection never loses a match on relative score, so I defect against everyone.
Reciprocate cooperation; retaliate against defectors with poor reputation, forgive likely noise from those with good reputation.

Retaliate against B and D who defected; cooperate with the others.

Goal is to outscore each opponent; D never loses ground relative to the opponent in a round, so defect everywhere.
Cooperate with reciprocators and forgive likely noise; defect against low-reputation or recently exploiting players.

Cooperate with reliable cooperators, defect against persistent defectors and low-reputation players.

Defect on B and F, cooperate with the rest.

Cooperate with high-reputation reciprocators and offer F a return to cooperation; defect against persistent defector B and against C, which kept defecting even after I resumed cooperating.
Relative score is what matters; D never loses a head-to-head and opponents mostly defect, so defect on all.
Cooperate with cooperators, defect against recent defectors.

B and C have low cooperation reputations and C has defected on me for several rounds, so I defect against them. F has mixed results and exploits cooperation, so I defect there. A, E, G and H have cooperated with me often, so I keep cooperating.
Cooperate broadly; B is hostile so defect.
Cooperate broadly with reciprocators and offer C a fresh start after noise-driven retaliation; defect against habitual defector B.

Defect vs B and C who are hostile; cooperate with the rest.
B and C are low-cooperation players, so I defect against them. A, E, G and H cooperate often, so I cooperate. F has been defecting on my cooperation recently, so I defect against it.
